sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Hotwire — Turbo + Stimulus — is the default frontend stack for Rails 7 and 8, and interviewers at Rails companies now expect you to understand it. Turbo Drive replaces full-page loads with fetch requests; Turbo Frames replace partial sections of the page; Turbo Streams push real-time DOM updates over WebSocket or SSE from the server. Stimulus adds small controllers that add behaviour to server-rendered HTML without the overhead of a SPA framework. This page covers all three layers: how they compose, the difference between Turbo Frames (synchronous request) and Turbo Streams (asynchronous push), when to use each, and the critical comparison interviewers always ask — when is Hotwire enough vs when should you reach for React or Vue.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: turbo-drive-frames, turbo-streams, stimulus-controllers, hotwire-vs-spa. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
